concerns.text: T001–T004 are all tagged [P] (parallel-safe) but form a strict producer→consumer chain: T002 iterates 'the streamed raw data' produced by T001; T003's few-shot examples are 'sampled from the corpus' produced by T002; T004 loads 'data/processed/corpus.csv' (T002) and 'the four prompt files' (T003). Running these in parallel violates producer-before-consumer. Remove the [P] tags or restructure so only genuinely independent tasks (e.g., T001 vs T003's zero-shot templates) are parallel.

T006's chi-square exclusion-independence test is described as 'exclusion vs. condition', but exclusion is determined by Python I/O extraction (T006) which runs before any condition-dependent data exists at that point in the flow; the test can only be computed after T007/T009 produce per-condition results. Clarify that the χ² is computed from the joint snippet×condition outcome table after validation, or move the test into T009/T010, to avoid an implementer computing it against data that does not yet exist.
